cards.subject: The Black Morass
lines: This was the northern half of an ancient swamp that existed long before the Dark Portal. The portal did not make it.
After the portal's destruction the southern half was scorched into the Blasted Lands, and the surviving north was renamed in honour of the dead of the Second War.

cards.subject: The Alliance has nothing here
lines: No town, no hub, no reason. In here the zone is Horde infrastructure and empty marsh.
Marshtide Watch, the Bloodmire and the whole faction war over this swamp are Cataclysm inventions.

cards.subject: Stonard
cards.tag: The orcs' first ground in this world
lines: Put up right after the Dark Portal opened, and named as one of the oldest orcish settlements on Azeroth.
This muddy handful of huts predates Orgrimmar, Durotar, and everything the Horde built after crossing the sea.

cards.subject: Rockard and Kyross
lines: Three orc outposts went up in the Black Morass. The First War destroyed two of them outright and left Stonard badly damaged.
Stonard is the only one you can walk into.
The other two are names in the lore with nothing on the map.

cards.subject: The only shaman trainer on the continent
lines: It holds the Eastern Kingdoms' only Horde shaman trainer, and the Horde's master alchemist besides.
For a shaman on this continent, this swamp is not optional.
It is one of very few reasons anybody came here on purpose rather than in transit.

cards.subject: Read the subzone names
cards.tag: And then go and look at them
lines: Splinterspear Junction. Sorrowmurk. Stagalbog. The Shifting Mire. Misty Valley.
Named places with almost nothing attached to any of them.
The names are better than the zone. This is a fully labelled map of an unbuilt place.

cards.subject: The Pool of Tears
lines: Landlocked, ringed by marsh. It only becomes a saltwater bay when Cataclysm cuts a channel to the Forbidding Sea.
The water you are standing in has no ocean in it — a detail that is wrong in every modern screenshot.

cards.subject: The thing sticking out of the lake
lines: The temple's upper structure breaks the surface, in an otherwise featureless marsh.
Atal'ai ruins lie scattered along the shore and across the lakebed, and artefacts can be recovered underwater.
Swim down and look at it before you go in.

cards.subject: The Atal'ai are refugees
lines: More than a thousand years ago a priest sect broke away from the collapsing Gurubashi Empire in Stranglethorn and fled north into this swamp.
Everything troll here is downstream of one exile march.
The temple is what they built when they reached somewhere nobody would look.

cards.subject: Ysera sank it
lines: The Atal'ai built the temple to summon Hakkar. Ysera found out and drowned the whole structure under the water with her green dragonflight.
It backfired. Sinking it hid the cult from the world.
Their work went on undisturbed underneath, for centuries.

cards.subject: The guard is still posted
lines: Green dragons were stationed here after the sinking and never stood down.
The Shade of Eranikus — what is left of Ysera's own lieutenant — is inside.
The watch set to contain the cult became one of the things you have to fight.
